comparisons.assumption: F releases one record and clears active frames after window four
comparisons.facts: Four windows, records set after the last window, phase released, finally clears active_call/call_anchor/entry/public.

comparisons.assumption: F source snapshots include original source adapter namespace
comparisons.facts: The source owner field exists before snapshot capture. The wire registry adds no adapter attribute.

comparisons.assumption: P and E remain released at eight windows
comparisons.facts: Producer checks terminal registrations, complete source relation, child completion and closed proof before F release.

comparisons.assumption: Graph snapshots retain Z ancestry and original graph objects
comparisons.facts: Snapshots capture the complete delegate ancestry. F retains Bf/If/Mf separately.

comparisons.assumption: F getter is proof access only
comparisons.facts: It checks record anchors. Wire admission uses an exact original-record preflight and never invokes this getter.

comparisons.assumption: Converter uses local copies and original predicate with no external callback
comparisons.facts: The six-key input triggers removal of tool_name and timestamp. Scalar values keep their identities.

comparisons.assumption: Actual transport needs no client setup
comparisons.facts: Neither class defines __init__ or __new__. Wire verifies constructor identity and class namespace anchors.
The stack is current -> _call -> _Admission.current -> wire.current. Wire permits only original F derive with parent Mf.
Wire routes only its registered derive frame. Clock callbacks do not call checkpoints or shared operations.

comparisons.assumption: Derived content retains restrictions after labels disappear
comparisons.facts: The original engine joins parent profiles before retention. Original selected grants remain mandatory at release.
